transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... my regular doctor told me I had to come. He says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I guess I can see my work pants hanging kind of loose on me lately, but... I don't know. Part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale goes down. I didn't really think I needed to be here.
Can you tell me about your eating habits lately? Have you been trying to eat less or avoid certain foods?

I guess... I mean, I still cook. I make plates for my husband and my mother-in-law every day. It's just... by the time I actually sit down, I... I don't know. I usually just tell myself that some coffee, or maybe a few vegetables, or half a piece of toast is enough for me.
Do you find yourself afraid of gaining weight or feeling like you need to lose more weight, even though others might see you as too thin?

I suppose... It's just, if I do eat something heavier, like the biscuits or pasta I make for them... I just get nervous. I spend the rest of the day scared that it's going to show on me. I catch myself checking my reflection in the glass while I'm cleaning the building... just thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
Have you ever made yourself sick or used laxatives, diet pills, or excessive exercise to try to control your weight?
No... no, I don't do any of that. I just... I just stay busy with work. Moving around the building all day is... it's enough. I don't take anything or... make myself sick.
Do you feel that your weight or body shape has a strong impact on how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself?

I guess... maybe. I just... when I manage to stay small, and... neat... I feel like I'm handling everything right. Like things are in order. But... if I happen to see my reflection and my stomach looks even a little bit full... I don't know. I just feel like I've let myself go. That's all.
When you look at yourself, do you worry more about your body weight or shape than most people do, or more than you think you should?
I'm not really sure. I don't... I don't know how much other people think about it. I just try to keep myself looking neat. I haven't really thought about whether it's... too much.
Would you say that how you see your body or your weight is one of the most important things that affects how you feel about yourself?

I suppose. I mean... like I said a minute ago. As long as I stay small, I feel like I'm handling things right. But if I catch my reflection and my stomach looks even the least bit full... I just feel like I've completely let myself go. So... yes. I guess it dictates a lot of how I feel.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself as heavier than you actually are?
I don't... I don't really know. I just... I see what's there. I don't think I'm making it up.

Do you ever find yourself eating a lot in a short period of time, more than most people would eat in similar circumstances, and then feel like you need to make up for it by restricting food or doing something else to prevent weight gain?
No. I don't... I don't ever eat a lot at once. I just... I don't do that. So there's nothing I'd need to make up for.
Would you say that your self-worth is largely tied to how you feel about your body weight or shape?

I... I think I just said that. Um... yeah. Like I mentioned, if I stay small and... neat, I feel like I'm doing okay. But if I see my stomach looking even a little full... I feel like I've completely failed. So... yes.
Have your concerns about your weight or body shape been affecting your ability to function normally in your daily life, like at work, with your family, or in social situations?

I... well, I still get my cleaning shifts done. I don't let it affect my work. But... I guess I don't really go to family dinners anymore. Or the meals after church. My husband says I'm... I'm there with everyone, but I'm not really joining in. I just... I prefer to keep to myself when there's food.
Even though others might see you as thin or underweight, do you still feel like you need to lose more weight or worry about becoming too heavy?

I... I don't know about needing to lose more. But I guess I do worry about getting heavy. If I... if I eat something heavier, like... a biscuit or some pasta... I just spend the rest of the day scared it's going to show on me. I end up... checking myself a lot. Just thinking I need to make up for it somehow.
Even though you're losing weight and others might see you as too thin, do you still feel like you need to keep your weight as low as possible or that gaining any weight would be terrible?

I... I wouldn't say I'm trying to keep it as low as possible. I don't really think of it that way. I just... I just want to stay how I am. Like I said, I just don't want to get heavy. I don't know if gaining a little would be terrible, exactly... I just... I'd rather not.
When you look at yourself, do you feel like certain parts of your body appear larger or heavier than they actually are, even if others might not see it that way?

I... I don't really know if I see things that aren't there. It's more just... well, if I can stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. But... if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even the least bit full... I just feel like I've completely let myself go.
Besides eating less and staying busy with work, do you ever take any other steps, like avoiding certain situations or changing your routine, to make sure you don’t gain weight?

I... well, I still get my cleaning shifts done. I make sure of that. But... I guess I don't really go to the family dinners anymore. Or the meals after church. My husband... he says I'm there with everyone, but I'm not really joining in. I just... it's easier that way.
Even if you don't think you're seeing things that aren't there, do you often feel like you look heavier than you actually are when you see yourself in the mirror or reflections?
I don't know... I don't really think about it like that. I just... I look in the mirror and I see what's there. I don't think I look heavy, exactly, I just... I see the parts that aren't right yet.
When you look at yourself, do you feel like your body weight or shape is more of a problem than others seem to think it is?

I... I don't know what other people think. My husband fusses, but... I don't see it as a problem. It's just... like I said before. If I keep myself small, and... neat... it just feels like I have things under control. Like I'm doing things right. But if I catch my reflection and my stomach looks even a little bit full... I just... I feel like I've completely let myself go. It just feels wrong.
